questions.question: A topology for a Local Area Network in which all nodes are individually connected to a central connection point like a hub or switch is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Star topology.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A topology for a Local Area Network in which all nodes are individually connected to a central connection point like a hub or switch is called Star Topology.**
 
• In a star topology, each device needs only one link and one I/O port to connect it to any number of other devices.
 
• Each device has a dedicated point-to-point link to a central controller known as a hub or switch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A multipoint connection is one in which more than two specific devices share a single link.
 
• A point-to-point connection provides a dedicated link between two devices. In mesh, star and ring topologies are point-to-point connection
 
• **Mesh topology:**
 
 
• In a mesh topology, every device has a dedicated point-to-point link to every other device.
 
 
 
• **Bus Topology**:
 
 
• In Bus Topology, one long cable acts as a backbone to link all the devices in a network.
 
 
 
• **Ring topology:**
 
 
• In a ring topology, each device has a dedicated point-to-point connection with only the two devices on either side of it; Each device is connected to its corresponding repeater.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Scanner.__**

__
 
• **The scanner is an input device**, which works more like a photocopy machine.
 
• It is a device that captures images from **photographic prints, posters, magazine pages.**
 
• The scanner captures images from the source which are then converted into a digital form that can be stored on the disk.
 
• These images can be edited before they are printed.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A monitor: **

 
 
• It is an output device that is used to display images, text, video, and graphics information generated by a connected computer.
 
• It is an output device that displays information in pictorial form.
 
• It is also known as a video display terminal (VDT) or a video display unit (VDU).
 
• The first computer monitor was introduced on 1 March 1973, which was part of the Xerox Alto computer system.
 
 
 
• **Projector:**
 
 
• A projector or image projector is an optical device that projects an image onto a surface, commonly a projection screen.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations launched the 'United for Biodiversity' coalition made up of zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens, national parks, natural history, and science museums from around the world, on World Wildlife Day 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__European Commission.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **European Commission** has launched the** 'United for Biodiversity'** coalition made up of zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens, national parks, natural history and science museums from around the world, on** World Wildlife Day 2020.**
 
• The European Commission has put forward plans for the world's first** "carbon border tax"** on imports of carbon-intensive goods, including steel, cement, fertilizers, and aluminium, as part of a program to meet its new climate target.
 
• The border levy should be phased in from** 2026.**
 
• The measure is designed to protect European industries from competitors abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Health Organization:**

 
 
• World Health Organization (WHO) is a** specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) established in 1948 **to further international cooperation for improved public health conditions.
 
• Although it inherited specific tasks relating to epidemic control, quarantine measures, and drug standardization from the** Health Organization of the League of Nations (set up in 1923) and the International Office of Public Health at Paris (established in 1907),** WHO was given a broad mandate under its constitution to promote the attainment of "the highest possible level of health" by all peoples.
 
• WHO defines health positively as **"a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity."**
 
• Each year WHO celebrates its date of establishment,** April 7, 1948, as World Health Day.**
 
• With administrative headquarters in **Geneva, governance of WHO operates through the World Health Assembly**, which meets annually as the general policy-making body, and through an Executive Board of health specialists elected for three-year terms by the assembly.
 
• **The WHO Secretariat,** which carries out routine operations and helps implement strategies, consists of experts, staff, and field workers who have appointments at the central headquarters or at one of the six regional WHO offices or other offices located in countries around the world.

questions.question: What is the importance of the ozone layer for life on Earth?

options.text: It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
It protects us from acidic rainfall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ozone layer is one of the layers in the earth's atmosphere inside the stratosphere layer. It absorbs ultraviolet radiation and protects people, animals, plants, and marine life from the sun's harmful rays.
 
• It was discovered by** Charles Fabry and Henri Buisson in 1913.**
 
• It can** absorb 98% of the sun's ultraviolet rays and almost 90% of ozone is located in the stratosphere layer at a distance of 15 to 30 km from the surface of Earth.**
 
• **In 1989, the Montreal protocol **came to protect the ozone layer by cutting the substances that deplete the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone:**

 
 
• It is important to mankind because it creates a protective coverage against ultraviolet rays.
 
• **Formula Ozone is O₃.**
 
• The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere. The stratosphere is the mass of protective gases clinging to our planet. The ozone layer acts as a shield for life on Earth.
 
• The ozone layer only makes **up 0.00006 per cent **of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The ozone layer is getting thinner because of chemicals called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). Due to this reason nowadays hydrochlorofluorocarbons **(HCFCs) are used in place of CFCs.**
 
• **CFCs are non-toxic, nonflammable chemicals containing atoms of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.**
 
• **"Ozone holes”** are popular names for areas of damage to the ozone layer.
 
• **The ozone layer is thinnest near the poles due to very low temperatures.**

questions.question: Who is the founder of the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Professor Muhammad Yunus.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi social entrepreneur, the Nobel Peace Prize awardee is the founder of the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh.**
 
• Grameen Banks have been created with the purpose of serving **rural areas with basic banking and financial services.**
 
• Grameen Banks** provide small loans** without the burden of high interest to those living in abject poverty to reduce the widespread rural poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In **2006** Grameen and Yunus were awarded the Nobel Prize for Peace.
 
• The Grameen model,** devised by Yunus in 1976, is based on groups of five prospective borrowers who meet regularly with Grameen Bank field managers**. Typically, two of the five prospective borrowers are granted loans. If, after a probationary time period, the first two borrowers meet the terms of repayment, then loans are granted to the remaining group members.
 
• Preer pressure acts as a replacement for traditional loan collateral.** Grameen became an independent bank in 1983; headquartered in Dhaka, Bangladesh, it has more than 2,200 branches in the country.**
 
• The Grameen model has come to** symbolize an efficient means of helping the poor** by providing them with opportunities to help themselves.
 
• More than** 97 per cent** of Grameen's loan recipients have been women.

questions.question: What was the meaning of ‘Ryot’ in British records in the 18th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Peasants.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ryotwari system** is one of the three principal methods of revenue collection in British India.
 
• It was prevalent in most of southern India, being the standard system of the Madras Presidency.
 
• The system was devised by **Capt. Alexander Read and Thomas Munro at the end of the 19th century and introduced by the latter when he was governor (1820-27) of Madras (now Chennai).**
 
• This was practised in the Madras and Bombay areas, as well as Assam and Coorg provinces.
 
• In this system, the peasants or cultivators were regarded as the owners of the land. They had ownership rights, could sell, mortgage, or gift the land.
 
• The rates were** 50% in dryland and 60% **in wetland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, who often oppressed villagers, and an assessment of the tax on land actually cultivated and not merely occupied.
 
• This system also gave much power to subordinate revenue officials, whose activities were inadequately supervised.
 
• **The name of the system comes from the word ryot, an Anglicization by the British in India of the Arabic word raīyah, meaning a peasant or cultivator.**
 
• The Arabic word passed into Persian (rakyat) was carried by the Mughals, who used it throughout India in their revenue administration.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a plateau situated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Maikal.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Maikal range is not a plateau situated in India.
 
• **The Maikal range:**
 
 
• They are located in the eastern part of the Satpuras range in Kawardha District of Chhattisgarh and Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Narmada, Mahanadi, and Son River originate through this range.
 
• The highest peak of this range is Mount Amarkantak.
 
• It is the broad topographical division located in Chhattisgarh.
 
• Kanha National Park is located in the Maikal Hills of the Satpuras region.
 
• The Baigas and the Gonds are two hilly tribes located here.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chota Nagpur Plateau:**

 
 
• It covers parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, and Chattisgarh.
 
• It has an elevation of 4430 feet.
 
• The Mahanadi River lies to the south and the Indo-Gangetic plain to the north.
 
• The total area is approximately 65000 square kilometers.
 
• The region is rich in resources like bauxite, iron ore, etc.
 
• Given below are the divisions of the Chota Nagpur Plateau:
 
• Pat region.
 
• Ranchi Plateau.
 
• Hazaribagh plateau.
 
• Koderma plateau.
 
• Damodar trough.
 
• Palamu.
 
• Manbhum-Singhbhum.
 
 
 
• **Malwa Range:**
 
 
• The Malwa Plateau is bounded by the Madhya Bharat Plateau and Bundelkhand Upland to the north, the Vindhya Range to the east and

 south, and the Gujarat Plains to the west.
 
• The plateau is located in western Madhya Pradesh and south-eastern Rajasthan with Gujarat in the west.
 
• Agar, Dewas, Dhar, Indore, Jhabua, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Rajgarh, Ratlam, Shajapur and Ujjain, Guna and Sehore districts of Madhya Pradesh, and the districts of Jhalawar and parts of Kota, Banswara, and Pratapgarh of Rajasthan are covered by the plateau.
 
• It was formed between 60 and 68 million years ago.
 
• Major rivers like Betwa, Mahi, Chambal, etc. are located here.
 
• The Simhasta Mela, which is held every 12 years is conducted on the banks of the Shipra river. The river is also located here.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Heavy rainfall.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Heavy rainfall is not an effect of an earthquake.
 
• Impacts of Earthquake:
 
 
• Earthquake Damage, Danger & Destruction. The destructive effects of earthquakes are Fissures, Collapse, landslides, tsunamis, fires, and fault rupture. The violent shaking of the ground produces the greatest property losses and personal injuries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tsunamis:**
 
 
• Water waves are caused by the sudden vertical movement of a large area of the seafloor during an undersea earthquake.
 
• Tsunamis are often called tidal waves, but this term is a misnomer.
 
• Unlike regular ocean tides, tsunamis are not caused by the tidal action of the Moon and Sun.
 
• The height of a tsunami in the deep ocean is typically about 1 foot, but the distance between wave crests can be very long more than 60 miles.
 
• The speed at which the tsunami travels decreases as water depth decreases. In the mid-Pacific, where the water depths reach 3 miles, tsunami speeds can be more than 430 miles per hour.

questions.question: Who among the following kings founded the Maurya empire in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chandragupta.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire**.
 
• He at the young age of 25, captured Pataliputra from the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, Dhanananda. In this task, he was assisted by **Kautilya**, who was also known as** Chanakya or Vishnugupta**.
 
• Located on the hills of Kaimur, the city of **Pavapuri**, also known as** Paava,** is located near** Rajgir and Bodh Gaya **in the Nalanda district of Bihar.
 
• This holy city for the followers of Jainism. Along with being the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, Vaishali is a city built out of Muzaffarpur Bihar. The main language here is** Vajjika.**
 
• **Kushinagar**, a city known as the** Parinirvana Sthal of Mahatma Buddha**, is located in the eastern frontier of Uttar Pradesh, whose former name is Kasia Bazaar.
 
• The dialect of common people is **Bhojpuri.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• With the help of Chanakya (Vishnugupta/ Kautilya), Chandragupta Maurya defeated Dhana Nanda (322 BCE) and founded the Mauryan Dynasty.
 
• Chanakya encouraged Chandragupta Maurya and his army to take over the throne of Magadha.
 
• His vast empire included** Bihar, Bengal, Deccan (except modern Kerala, Tamilnadu, and parts of Northeast India), Eastern Afghanistan, Baluchistan, and the area west of the Indus river.**

questions.question: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Vice-President of India.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vice President of India is the ex-officio chairman of Rajya Sabha.**
 
• The Chairman presides over the sessions of Rajya Sabha while the Deputy Chairman takes care of the day-to-day matters of the house in the absence of the Chairman.
 
• The present chairman of **Rajya Sabha is **Jagdeep Dhankhar.
 
• Rajya Sabha is the upper house of parliament that represents the states and union territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rajya Sabha is a** permanent body and not subject to dissolution.**
 
• Rajya Sabha currently has a maximum membership of** 245**. The maximum strength of the Rajyasabha is fixed at 250 (if the question asked 'Maximum Strength', the answer would be 250).
 
• Among its 245 members, 233 are elected by the legislatures of the states and union territories using single transferable votes through Open Ballot while the remaining 12 members are appointed by the President for their contributions to art, literature, science, and social services.
 
• **One-third **of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years. Rajya Sabha represents the federal character of the constitution.
